cards.note: Wide black and yellow striped guy-wires are commonly found in Chubu. Be aware that these are also found in Okinawa

It's relatively easy to distinguish Okinawa from Chubu, and doing so can earn you valuable points. While both regions use the same type of guy-wire, Okinawa uses straight-lined reflectors, in contrast to Chubu's twisted reflectors.
Orange or yellow guy-wires with and obvious bulge close to the ground are found in Chugoku. They can also be found in single-wire versions.
Kyushu-style guy-wires are easy to spot by their “paddle” shape, unlike the “bottle” or “baseball bat” shapes of Southern styles. They sometimes can have two thin wires joining a thick base.

Kyushu guy-wires are also found in Okinawa, which makes them hard to tell apart—especially since both regions use the same reflector pads. Because this can cost or earn you a lot of points in later rounds, I still wanted to give you a way to differentiate them. That’s where this pole plate meta comes in. Fortunately, it’s one of the simplest and most recognizable: it's the only one with horizontal bars between the characters, and it's exclusive to Okinawa. This basically makes the guy-wire meta secondary, but it’s still a useful clue that you might be in Okinawa and should check the pole plate.

Northern-style guy-wires have a smooth, cylindrical cover with yellow and black stripes. There are two types—thin and thick—and while both appear in the same regions, their distribution may vary slightly. They're mostly found in northern Japan, except for Shikoku, which is an outlier with mixed styles.

Shikoku Guy-Wires are usually either Northern or Wa-To types, but what sets them apart is their pairing with the Shikoku pole reflector pad—a short pad with six clear stripes. This combo is a strong sign you're in Shikoku. Be careful not to mix it up with the similar Kansai reflector, which is longer and often faded in color.

Tohokur Guy-Wires are a unique variant of the Northern style, featuring a distinct bulge near the ground. This shape gives them a mixed appearance, combining elements of both Northern and Chugoku guy-wires. They're only found in the Tohoku region of Japan, where their unusual shape makes them easy to identify despite some similarities to nearby styles. From a distance, they may be confused with Northern guy-wires, but the bulge near the bottom sets them apart up close.

Wa-To guy-wires have a distinctive bottle shape with yellow-black stripes and can be easily distinguished from similar types when viewed up close. They are mainly found in western and central Japan – from Wakayama to Toyama – as well as throughout Shikoku, where they are less common but still present everywhere.
